name: Asenora

attributes.attribute: thrown into the sea in a barrel while pregnant
carved in St. Senara's church and perhaps a sea goddess
mother of Perseus and source of a parallel motif

sources: Straffon, Cheryl. The Earth Goddess: Celtic and Pagan Legacy of the Landscape. London: Blandford, 1997, 85.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Asenora was a Cornish heroine. A legend in Cornwall tells her story. She was a princess of Brittany. Someone threw her into the sea in a barrel while she was pregnant. The barrel drifted to Ireland. She was rescued there. She tried to return to Brittany. She only got as far as Zenor. There she founded a church. People honor her there as St. Senara. A famous carving sits in that church. The carving is 600 years old. It shows a mermaid. The mermaid may have been a sea goddess. The motif may come from the Greek story of Danae, mother of Perseus. Unlike the Greek version, Asenora is the center of the Cornish tale. The legend says nothing about her unborn offspring.

key_results: Document Asenora as a Cornish heroine from a Breton princess.
Record her rescue, church at Zenor, and veneration as St. Senara.
Note the parallel with Danae and Perseus.
